root_cause.text: The remove() function unconditionally returned early if pm_runtime_resume_and_get() failed, bypassing the cleanup of the SPI controller and other resources, causing a resource leak.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "The remove() callback returned early if pm_runtime_resume_and_get() failed, skipping the cleanup of spi controller and other resources." The patch removes the `if (ret < 0) return;` block, ensuring cleanup always executes regardless of PM resume result.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure stm32_ospi_remove always cleans up the SPI controller regardless of pm_runtime_resume_and_get success.
intent_record.what: Removed the return value check and early return from pm_runtime_resume_and_get call in stm32_ospi_remove, now calling it unconditionally.
intent_record.how: Previously, a failure to resume runtime PM would cause the remove function to return early without unregistering the SPI controller. Now, even if pm_runtime_resume_and_get fails, the function proceeds to unregister the controller and complete cleanup.

grouping_result.intent: Ensure stm32_ospi_remove always cleans up the SPI controller regardless of pm_runtime_resume_and_get success.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by ensuring the cleanup of the SPI controller is performed regardless of the success of pm_runtime_resume_and_get, preventing the resource leak.

candidates.rationale: This early return statement causes the function to exit without calling spi_unregister_controller and other cleanup when pm_runtime_resume_and_get fails, leading to a resource leak.
